title: Multi-chain network model for liveness (statement sketch) -- SKIP recommendation
goal_statement: Sketch, additively, a network layer in which each of n honest producers holds its own locally-adopted chain (adopted via the existing MoltPetit.Model.selectChain, which today has no theorem about it anywhere in the repo), honest blocks are delivered to the next honest producer within their slot, and prove that under those hypotheses every honest producer's adopted chain equals the single canonical run MoltPetit.Model.buildChain g ss -- i.e. discharge the single-chain premise that liveness_global / Molt.global_liveness currently assumes by fiat (the run literally IS buildChain g ss; MoltPetit/Model/Liveness.lean:361-372), rather than proving anything new about validChain or safety. This targets exactly the sentence at paper/molt.tex:1203-1205: "a fully multi-chain network model is future work."

new_files.outline: namespace MoltPetit.Model.Network (name-clash-checked clean: netRun, netStep, Adversary, Views, honestSlots, adoptAll, Network do not exist anywhere in the repo -- W7-run2.md transcript line 36). import MoltPetit.Model.Liveness (brings Definitions, Model, Safety, Soundness transitively). Sections: (1) Views := NodeId -> Chain, one entry per honest producer id (NodeId := Nat, abbrev), holding the chain that producer has currently adopted via selectChain. (2) NAMED DESIGN DECISION (fixes finding: List.foldl typing): netStep n views slot delivered : Views -- deliberately DROPS newId/contentsHash/keyIndex as separate parameters and instead hardcodes the same convention buildFrom already uses at Liveness.lean:296-297 (`nextBlock s s 0 0 tip`, i.e. newId := slot, contentsHash := 0, keyIndex := 0) internally, exactly so the blocks netStep manufactures are structurally identical (same id/contentsHash/keyIndex fields) to buildChain's blocks -- required for single_view_eq_buildChain's equality to even typecheck as true, since Block equality is structural. The producer of `slot` extends its own current view with nextBlock slot slot 0 0 tip and folds the result back through selectChain n (views (producerForSlot n slot)) (extended candidate); every OTHER honest node's view is updated by adoptAll: selectChain n against whatever it received this slot (trivial no-op unless a delivery hypothesis supplies a candidate -- this is where 'honest blocks reach the next honest producer within their slot' has to be threaded through as an explicit function argument, not discovered). (3) netRun n g ss delivered : Views -- SPELLED OUT EXPLICITLY (fixes finding: the previous draft wrote `List.foldl netStep (fun _ => [g]) ss`, which does not typecheck because List.foldl expects f : β → α → β and netStep as previously drafted took five extra explicit arguments beyond (n, views)): `List.foldl (fun views s => netStep n views s (delivered ss s)) (fun _ => [g]) ss`. With netStep's signature narrowed to (n, views, slot, delivered) as above, `fun views s => netStep n views s (delivered ss s)` has exactly type Views -> Nat -> Views, which is what List.foldl needs when folding over ss : List Nat with accumulator Views -- this now typechecks as literally written. (4) Adversary -- an uninterpreted ByzantineSlots-indexed family of competitor chains a corrupt producer may broadcast instead of building on the honest tip; NOT modeled in this sketch (see risks: without it the theorem below is not a genuine strengthening of the existing single-chain liveness_global, only a restatement). (5) Target theorem single_view_eq_buildChain (see new_theorems) -- the deliverable this whole file exists for. Size if built straight, WITHOUT an adversary: ~150-220 lines (Views/netStep/netRun plumbing ~60, delivery hypothesis threading ~40, the equality induction on ss mirroring buildChain_map_slot/buildFrom's structural recursion ~60-90). Size WITH a genuine adversary (competitor chains, fork-choice reasoning via no_deep_fork/LastCommonHeight to show selectChain converges all honest views onto one chain even when Byzantine producers broadcast alternatives): 500-900 lines and a new agreement engine, not a restatement -- this is the real content the paper sentence is gesturing at, and it is the expensive part.

New axiom-guard file (MoltPetit/Results/Axioms.lean is NOT edited, per the additive-only constraint). import MoltPetit.Model.Network. One `/-- info: 'MoltPetit.Model.Network.<thm>' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/ #guard_msgs in #print axioms MoltPetit.Model.Network.<thm>` block per headline (single_view_eq_buildChain at minimum; more if the adversary variant is built). ~15-40 lines. Registered in the default build by ONE new import line added to MoltPetit.lean (the only permitted existing-file touch besides Molt.lean).

new_defs.name: Views
new_defs.meaning: One adopted chain per honest producer id (id = slot % n, i.e. producerForSlot n slot for some slot -- indexed 0..n-1). The multi-chain state the model must carry that buildChain (a single Chain) does not.

new_defs.name: netStep
new_defs.signature: def netStep (n : Nat) (views : Views) (slot : Nat) (delivered : NodeId -> Option Chain) : Views
new_defs.meaning: One slot of the network: the producer of `slot` extends its own view via nextBlock slot slot 0 0 (views (producerForSlot n slot)).getLast! + selectChain (recovering produceBlock?'s logic per-node instead of globally); every other node j adopts selectChain n (views j) (delivered j) if `delivered j` gives it something, else keeps views j. NAMED DESIGN DECISION (added to address the fold-typing finding): newId := slot, contentsHash := 0, keyIndex := 0 are hardcoded inside netStep, NOT threaded as separate parameters -- this is exactly buildFrom's own convention (`nextBlock s s 0 0 tip`, Liveness.lean:296-297), adopted deliberately so the Block fields netStep produces are structurally identical to buildChain's, which single_view_eq_buildChain's conclusion (a literal Chain equality) requires. Dropping these three parameters from netStep's signature (versus an earlier draft that kept them as explicit arguments) is also what makes `fun views s => netStep n views s (delivered ss s)` fit List.foldl's expected `Views -> Nat -> Views` shape in netRun below. `delivered` is left an explicit function argument on purpose -- it is the formal home of 'honest blocks reach the next honest producer within their slot' (paper's Assumption 6 / ass:delivery), and how strong a hypothesis on it the target theorem needs is exactly the open design question this sketch cannot resolve without being built.

new_defs.name: netRun
new_defs.signature: def netRun (n : Nat) (g : Block) (ss : List Nat) (delivered : List Nat -> Nat -> NodeId -> Option Chain) : Views := List.foldl (fun views s => netStep n views s (delivered ss s)) (fun _ => [g]) ss
new_defs.meaning: The fold wrapper is now spelled out explicitly (fixes the finding: `List.foldl netStep (fun _ => [g]) ss` as previously drafted does not typecheck since netStep took five extra explicit arguments beyond (n, views), which List.foldl's binary step-function shape (Views -> Nat -> Views) cannot accommodate). With netStep narrowed to (n, views, slot, delivered), `fun views s => netStep n views s (delivered ss s)` has type Views -> Nat -> Views given n and delivered fixed, matching List.foldl's requirement exactly. `delivered` supplies, at each step, what each node received. The multi-node analogue of buildChain g ss (Liveness.lean:294).

new_theorems.name: single_view_eq_buildChain
hypotheses: hChain : List.IsChain (· < ·) (g.slot :: ss)  -- same schedule shape liveness_global already requires
hBudget : the same run-span-scoped ByzantineBounded hypothesis liveness_global takes (Liveness.lean:361, third hyp)

hDelivery : an explicit synchrony hypothesis on `delivered` -- e.g. `forall i s j, s in ss -> j = producerForSlot n (next slot after s) -> delivered ss s j = some (<the chain containing the block just produced at slot s>)` -- the exact shape is the real unknown; the salvage found NO existing List.IsPrefix/take/dropLast lemma in the core files to build this from, so it would be authored from scratch

hNoByzantineCompetitor : (SKETCH ONLY, not discharged here) every producer of every slot in ss is honest and follows netStep -- i.e. this sketch's theorem is stated WITHOUT an adversary, so it is a restatement of buildChain's construction through the Views/netStep plumbing, not a new agreement result
new_theorems.conclusion: forall j, j < n -> netRun n g ss delivered j = buildChain g ss
new_theorems.proof_sketch: Step 0 (NAMED DESIGN DECISION, added to address the fold-typing finding): netRun is unfolded to its explicit wrapper `List.foldl (fun views s => netStep n views s (delivered ss s)) (fun _ => [g]) ss`, and netStep's internal use of nextBlock slot slot 0 0 tip (newId := slot, contentsHash := keyIndex := 0) is recognized as literally buildFrom's own convention (`nextBlock s s 0 0 tip`, Liveness.lean:296-297) -- this is what makes the two sides of the target equality talk about structurally identical Block values at each step, rather than merely isomorphic ones; without adopting exactly this convention the conclusion `netRun n g ss delivered j = buildChain g ss` would be false as stated (mismatched id/contentsHash/keyIndex fields), since Block equality is structural. Step 1+: induction on ss mirroring buildFrom's own recursion (Liveness.lean:289, 296-335): at each step netStep either extends the unique honest producer's view (matches buildChain's nextBlock exactly by construction, per Step 0) or adopts via selectChain, which chooses candidate over cur only if candidate validates and is strictly longer (Definitions.lean:141) -- under hDelivery the only candidate ever offered IS the just-extended buildChain prefix, so selectChain always returns it once validChain holds, which reduces to liveness_valid_extension (Liveness.lean:232) supplying the validity side per step. WITHOUT an adversary this is genuinely just unfolding netStep to buildFrom's recursion -- the delivery hypothesis has to already say 'the thing delivered is definitionally the honest tip', which is close to assuming the conclusion. This is the sketch's central finding: the interesting case (Byzantine producers broadcasting a rival chain, forcing selectChain to genuinely discriminate) is exactly the case this proof sketch does NOT cover, and covering it is a multi-hundred-line addition (see new_files/Network.lean outline), not a corollary.

reuses.name: liveness_valid_extension
reuses.how: supplies validChain n (extended chain) = true at each honest step, feeding selectChain's validation guard

reuses.name: buildChain_map_slot
reuses.how: identifies the slot sequence netStep walks with the one buildChain walks, needed to line up the induction

reuses.name: MoltPetit.Model.selectChain
reuses.how: the adoption rule netStep calls at every non-producer node; this sketch would be the FIRST theorem anywhere about plain selectChain (confirmed absent by the salvage's grep -- Molt.selectChain bridges to selectCertifiedChain, a different function, per Molt/Verifier.lean:136-195)

reuses.name: liveness_global
reuses.how: the theorem this item's premise (a single canonical chain) currently discharges by definition; single_view_eq_buildChain would let liveness_global be re-derived per-node as `forall j < n, validChain n (netRun n g ss delivered j) = true` by rewriting through this equality -- a corollary, not a strengthening of liveness_global's conclusion

touches_existing.change: add one import line: `import MoltPetit.Model.Network` (or `import MoltPetit.Results.AxiomsNetwork`, which transitively imports Network) so `lake build` / `nix run .#verify-lean` actually elaborate the new file -- confirmed by the salvage: with no `roots`/`globs` in the four lean_lib stanzas, a file nothing imports is silently skipped by the default build.
touches_existing.why_unavoidable: explicitly permitted by the owner's constraints (root-module import lines are the one allowed touch); there is no additive way to get the default build to see a new top-level file.

paper_changes.change: Only if the FULL (adversary-bearing) version were built, not this sketch's restatement: soften or remove "a fully multi-chain network model is future work" (grep-able phrase: "fully multi-chain network model is future work") and add a one-line pointer to the new theorem, e.g. inside Theorem~\ref{thm:live}'s surrounding prose or as a following remark citing `MoltPetit.Model.Network.single_view_eq_buildChain` (or its adversary-bearing successor). Do NOT touch this for the restatement-only version built by this sketch's proof_sketch -- it would not honestly discharge the sentence's claim (no adversary, no genuine multi-chain convergence argument).

effort_sessions: 4-6 sessions for the version that actually earns the paper change (adversary + fork-choice convergence via no_deep_fork/LastCommonHeight); 1 session for the restatement-only sketch above, which is honest but nearly worthless (see risks)

risks.risk: The cheap version (no adversary) reduces to an near-tautological unfold of netStep into buildFrom's own recursion once hDelivery is strong enough to pin down what gets delivered -- it does not touch selectChain's actual discriminating behavior (candidate vs cur when both validate) at all, so it does not honestly discharge the paper's 'future work' sentence even though it is a true, axiom-clean, additive theorem.
risks.mitigation: Do not claim the paper change unless the adversary-bearing version is built. State this explicitly in any future work item spawned from this sketch.

risks.risk: The expensive version needs a genuine competitor-chain / adversary model and a fork-choice convergence argument built on no_deep_fork (MoltPetit/Model/Safety.lean:134) and LastCommonHeight (Definitions.lean:521) -- machinery designed for two ARBITRARY valid chains from a shared record, not for 'the chains selectChain would actually produce under repeated adoption'. Reusing it correctly (rather than re-deriving convergence from scratch) is itself a design problem this sketch has not solved.
risks.mitigation: A follow-up item, if ever taken, should spend its first session on exactly this reduction before writing any Network.lean code.

risks.risk: No List.IsPrefix / take / dropLast lemmas exist anywhere in the core files (confirmed by grep in the salvage) -- any argument that two nodes' adopted chains share a growing common prefix has to build this machinery from CommonPrefixUpTo (Definitions.lean:517) and exists_lastCommonHeight (Safety.lean:217), which were designed for a two-chain snapshot comparison, not an inductive per-slot convergence argument.
risks.mitigation: Budget this as its own sub-lemma set (~100-150 lines) if the expensive version is ever attempted.

alternatives_rejected.alt: State single_view_eq_buildChain over Molt.selectChain / Molt.produceBlock? (the paper-facing Verifier.lean names) instead of the core MoltPetit.Model.selectChain.
alternatives_rejected.why: Molt.selectChain bridges (via selectChain_eq_core, Verifier.lean:191-195) to MoltPetit.Model.selectCertifiedChain, a DIFFERENT function from the plain selectChain this item is about; building on the Molt side would silently change which selection rule is being modeled and would need its own bridge lemma, adding scope without adding value for a sketch.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Build the full adversary-bearing version now instead of sketching.
alternatives_rejected.why: Out of scope for a SKETCH item by the task's own instruction, and the planner's working hypothesis (4-6 sessions, low value for the paper's safety claims) is confirmed by this pass: the payoff is one sentence in the limitations-adjacent prose of a liveness theorem the paper already states and cites; no other work item or safety claim depends on it.

open_questions_for_owner: Is the paper sentence at molt.tex:1203-1205 ('a fully multi-chain network model is future work') something a reviewer is actually expected to push on, or is it acceptable as permanent scope-fencing? This changes the recommendation from skip to attempt.

If ever attempted, should the delivery hypothesis (`delivered`) be phrased over real slots or over the record/stamp-slot convention used by HonestBlocksCover et al.? The salvage flags this exact ambiguity (bad-reading note in Definitions.lean section) as unresolved for ANY module mixing TimedExecution-style real-slot semantics with the HonestBlocksCover-style stamped-slot convention -- W7 would be the first place the choice has to be made explicitly for a per-node (not per-window) delivery predicate.
hypothesis_verdict: CONFIRMED. The planner's working hypothesis holds up under inspection: a genuine multi-chain convergence theorem (one that actually exercises selectChain's discriminating behavior against Byzantine competitor chains, using no_deep_fork/LastCommonHeight) is a large new layer at 4-6 sessions, and it buys exactly one paper sentence (molt.tex:1203-1205) with no downstream effect on any safety theorem or any other work item. The cheap alternative (restating buildChain through a Views/netStep wrapper with no adversary) is buildable in ~1 session but is close to vacuous -- it does not discharge the paper's claim and would be dishonest to cite as doing so.
recommendation: SKIP, matching the planner's working hypothesis. Do not build even the cheap restatement-only version: it produces an axiom-clean, additive, real theorem, but its only fair use is 'we could technically cite a Lean name here', and citing it against the molt.tex:1203-1205 sentence without the adversary would overstate what was proved. If a reviewer specifically pushes on liveness/multi-chain in review, re-open this item and budget the full 4-6 sessions for the adversary-bearing version (Network.lean's Adversary component, un-sketched here) rather than building the restatement first and expanding it -- the restatement's netStep/Views plumbing is not obviously reusable once a real adversary and fork-choice convergence argument are added (the delivery-hypothesis shape almost certainly has to change), so building it now would not save time later and could create the exact kind of redo-loop the task's no-loops constraint is meant to prevent.

changes_made: [major, finding 1] Confirmed by direct inspection: List.foldl requires f : beta -> alpha -> beta, but the prior draft's netStep took five explicit arguments beyond (n, views) (slot, newId, contentsHash, keyIndex, delivered), so `List.foldl netStep (fun _ => [g]) ss` as literally written does not typecheck. Also confirmed buildFrom (Liveness.lean:289, 296-297) hardcodes `nextBlock s s 0 0 tip`, i.e. newId := s (the slot), contentsHash := 0, keyIndex := 0 -- a convention the design never stated, which the target theorem's literal Chain/Block equality silently depended on (Block equality is structural, so mismatched id/contentsHash/keyIndex fields would make single_view_eq_buildChain false as stated). Fixed by: (a) narrowing netStep's signature to (n, views, slot, delivered), dropping newId/contentsHash/keyIndex as separate parameters and instead hardcoding the buildFrom convention (nextBlock slot slot 0 0 tip) inside netStep's own definition -- named explicitly as a design decision in new_defs/netStep's meaning and in new_files/Network.lean's outline section (2); (b) spelling out netRun's fold wrapper explicitly as `List.foldl (fun views s => netStep n views s (delivered ss s)) (fun _ => [g]) ss`, which now typechecks because `fun views s => netStep n views s (delivered ss s)` has exactly type Views -> Nat -> Views once netStep is narrowed as in (a); (c) adding this as an explicit Step 0 in single_view_eq_buildChain's proof_sketch, ahead of the induction, so the equality's structural dependence on the convention is stated rather than assumed. No other part of the design changes: the theorem's hypotheses, conclusion, reuses, risks, recommendation (SKIP), and paper_changes are unaffected -- this was a plumbing/typing fix to the sketch's own internal consistency, not a change to what the sketch claims to prove or to its cost/value assessment.
